cases.description: A JSON object between the --- delimiters is valid YAML 1.2, so its members are the root's fields.
A # line inside the front matter is a YAML comment, not a level-1 heading, so the heading after the front matter is the record's only level-1 heading and gives the root's $title.
The front matter ends at the next --- line, so --- inside a quoted YAML value neither closes it nor reaches the body.
Without a title heading the root's fields still come from the front matter, and the root's $body is the text between the front matter and the first heading.

A --- line after a blank line is not at the very start of the file, so it is a thematic break, and the next --- line makes 'status: Open' a setext heading (CommonMark 0.31.2, 4.1 and 4.3); the record has no fields, and the root's $body is the text before the first heading.
The front matter's members are the root section's, and $key on a section is a $ member where none is allowed, so the record fails parse.
Front matter without a closing delimiter is a structural error at the root, rather than a thematic break followed by prose.
A ... line is not a delimiter, although Jekyll accepts it, so front matter closed only by ... is unclosed.
A delimiter line is --- optionally followed by spaces or tabs, so both lines delimit.
A delimiter is --- at the start of a line, so an indented --- inside a block scalar is part of the value.
Empty front matter gives the root no fields.
Front matter holding only a YAML comment is empty, and gives the root no fields.
Front matter holding a YAML sequence is not an object, which is data-block-not-object at the root.
Front matter holding a plain scalar is not an object, which is data-block-not-object at the root.
Front matter holding an unclosed flow sequence does not parse, which is a syntax error about the whole record, so at the root.
A UTF-8 byte order mark at the start of the file is skipped, so the front matter after it still starts the file.

The section members $title, $anchor, $tags, $body and $sections at the top of front matter are each dollar-member, since a Markdown root's title, anchor, tags, body and sections have their own syntax.
$schema at the top of front matter is the root's $schema, stored data that vmd does not interpret.
Another $ member at the top of front matter may be a section member of a newer minor version, so it is feature-unsupported at the member.
